detections.evidence_quote: the 'crunchy mama' movement, which is like the 'maha mama' movement
detections.summary: A listener letter mocks the 'crunchy mama'/MAHA mama parenting movement and its health claims about sunscreen, raw milk, seed oils and vaccines, and the hosts discuss why this social-media 'mama sphere' peer pressure catches on.

detections.evidence_quote: the natural sunscreens they praise still chemicals, just with friendlier names
detections.summary: Mocks anti-sunscreen sentiment among 'crunchy moms,' arguing natural sunscreens are still chemicals and that skipping SPF risks skin cancer from UV exposure.

detections.evidence_quote: Your raw milk isn't medicine; it's a bacterial gamble with splash.
detections.summary: Rebuts the idea that 'food from the earth' is automatically safe, arguing raw milk carries a bacterial risk rather than being medicine.

detections.evidence_quote: they treat seed oils like CIA mind control, but will slather their babies in beef tallow whipped with rose quartz energy
detections.summary: Mocks demonization of seed oils as food villains while the same group uses beef tallow as a skin product.

detections.evidence_quote: they treat seed oils like CIA mind control
detections.summary: A one-line joke attributes to the mocked group the belief that seed oils function like deliberate mind control.

detections.evidence_quote: an Amazon cart full of anti-vax books
detections.summary: Passing mention of 'anti-vax books' as part of characterizing the mocked parenting movement as pseudoscience and public-health sabotage.

detections.evidence_quote: I don't put chemicals on my kids.
detections.summary: Rebuts a chemical-purity claim ('I don't put chemicals on my kids') by pointing out everything, including water and the body, is made of chemicals.

detections.evidence_quote: I only feed my kids food from the earth
detections.summary: Mocks appeals to naturalness ('food from the earth,' raw milk, avoiding seed oils) as praised by the parenting movement.

detections.evidence_quote: people start to believe that they know more than science
detections.summary: Speaker argues a growing social-media peer pressure leads people to believe they know more than science.

detections.evidence_quote: Gen Z is depressed and anxious
detections.summary: Passing reference to reports that Gen Z is depressed and anxious, blamed on parental overinvolvement.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Ultraviolet radiation damages skin cells and poses a cancer risk when sunscreen is not used.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Meanwhile, ultraviolet radiation—literal sun poison—is cooking your skin cells like bacon.
verification_candidates.rationale: The claim that UV radiation damages skin cells and drives skin-cancer risk is checkable against dermatology evidence.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Raw milk carries a risk of bacterial contamination and is not a medicine.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Your raw milk isn't medicine; it's a bacterial gamble with splash.
verification_candidates.rationale: The claim that raw milk poses a bacterial safety risk is checkable against food-safety evidence.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Reports indicate that Gen Z has high rates of depression and anxiety.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: these reports that Gen Z is depressed and anxious
verification_candidates.rationale: A prevalence claim about Gen Z mental health attributed to unspecified reports could be checked against survey data.
